topology: R1 AS65001 - R2 AS65002 - R3 AS65003 - R4 AS65004. PC1 uses R1 client LAN, PC2 is the independent R2 local control, and SRV1 uses the R4 service LAN. Only R1 originates 192.168.10.0/24 and R4 originates 192.168.40.0/24. No IGP, default or static service routes. R2/R3 have prepared Loopback0 addresses for a bounded multihop exercise.
implemented: Twenty-seventh ENARSI entry: independent practice/reference documents, seven-row plan, staged ordinary IOS/Windows guide and deployment-origin/path/query permalinks. Existing UI, themes, icons, terminal styling and offline single-HTML use remain unchanged.

Initial R2 expects remote-AS 65030 for R3, which actually uses AS65003. Four leaf directed sessions remain Established; central transport cannot complete a valid BGP exchange. Both service directions fail while both PC2/R2 controls work. Actual failed probes and controls earn diagnosis.

Repaired baseline has six real directed BGP sessions with received OPEN/KEEPALIVE over persistent modeled TCP179. External routes install at AD20. R1 service AS path is 65002 65003 65004; R4 client path is 65003 65002 65001. External next hops are rewritten at each boundary. Actual requests traverse all four routers and complete HTTP responses return to PC1.

Six incidents cover wrong remote AS, neighbor administrative shutdown with interface still up, one-sided key mismatch, outbound prefix-list deny with sessions still Established, a nonmatching /25 network statement over a connected /24, and loopback peer migration. Each requires failed service plus working independent controls and fresh restored traffic.

Loopback migration uses only reciprocal static /32 peer routes. Default single-hop sessions remain Idle despite successful loopback ping; ebgp-multihop 2 with update-source Loopback0 on both sides restores real transport and recursive BGP forwarding. Grading requires failed default, working multihop service and final return to the original physical pair. Static service/default shortcuts are rejected.

Engine correction: default single-hop external peers must be directly connected on an operational interface in the same address family/VRF. Explicit multihop bypasses this check while honoring actual wire TTL; internal BGP and TTL security retain their prior paths. Added missing help/Tab grammar for the already implemented peer password command.

Seven live checks and nine observed checks; practice0, diagnosis1, baseline10, full16, reference seven live only. Three distinct correlated original requests/replies in every required direction, actual No route drops for failures and completed TCP HTTP. Configuration-only, stale, partial and skipped intermediate multihop evidence fail. YAML retains earned history and rebuilds protocol state.
scope: IOS IPv4 unicast eBGP for this four-AS topology, logical BGP messages over modeled TCP, peer key matching, prefix-list export, exact origination, AS paths, next hops and loopback multihop. Native checks include actual TCP179 blocking/hold expiry, matching keys, hard reset, rendered replay and saved reload. No fresh CML capture is claimed. Authentication is modeled key matching, not wire TCP-MD5 cryptography; this is not complete binary RFC4271 or multiprotocol interoperability certification.
